- Use the existing project framework and component architecture where possible.

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Create a modern B2B SaaS support/helpdesk interface inspired by high-quality products such as Linear, Intercom, Zendesk, Notion, and modern admin dashboards.

Visual style:
- Clean
- Premium
- Minimal
- Professional
- Slightly warm rather than sterile
- Excellent typography
- Subtle borders
- Soft shadows
- Rounded corners
- Strong spacing system
- Clear information hierarchy
- Lots of intentional whitespace, but eliminate the excessive empty space currently visible
- Avoid huge typography
- Avoid bulky cards
- Avoid overly decorative gradients

OVERALL LAYOUT:

Create a proper application shell:

1. LEFT SIDEBAR
   - Fixed/collapsible sidebar
   - Support Desk logo/icon at top
   - Workspace name
   - Navigation:
     - Inbox
     - All Tickets
     - My Tickets
     - Open
     - Pending
     - Resolved
     - Analytics
     - Settings
   - Show ticket counts as subtle badges
   - Highlight the active navigation item
   - User/profile section at bottom
   - Use clean icons
   - Sidebar should feel compact and professional

2. TOP HEADER
   - Breadcrumb:
     Support Desk / Tickets / TICKET-123
   - Search button/input
   - Notification icon
   - User avatar
   - Optional keyboard shortcut indicator
   - Keep header compact

3. MAIN TICKET AREA

Replace the current enormous:
"Issue with Attendance"

with a much more refined ticket header.

Header should contain:

   TICKET-123
   Issue with Attendance

   Status badge
   Priority badge
   Created date
   Last updated

Example hierarchy:

   TICKET-1024
   Issue with Attendance

   [Open] [High Priority]

   Not able to mark my attendance on the portal

Make the ticket title around 28–34px, NOT huge.

4. TICKET METADATA

Instead of the current large right-side card, create a compact metadata section.

Display:

   Priority       High
   Assignee       HR
   Created        Sep 24, 2026
   Updated        Sep 24, 2026

Use small labels and strong values.

Use icons where appropriate.

5. DESCRIPTION

Create a clean section:

   DESCRIPTION

   Not able to mark my attendance on the portal

Don't make this section unnecessarily tall.

6. STATUS / ACTION BAR

Make the current:

   Change status
   [Select next status]
   [Update status]

look like a proper action toolbar.

Example:

   Status
   [ Open ▼ ]

   [Update status]

Add:
- Loading state
- Disabled state
- Success feedback/toast
- Error feedback
- Smooth hover/focus states

The primary action button should be visually strong but not oversized.

7. CONVERSATION

This is currently the weakest part of the UI.

Turn it into a proper support conversation timeline.

Header:

   Conversation
   0 comments

For messages/comments, design proper chat-style timeline entries:

   Avatar
   Kiran
   Sep 24, 2026 at 7:20 PM

   Comment text...

For different users, visually distinguish authors subtly.

Add vertical timeline styling where appropriate.

8. ADD COMMENT

Replace the giant plain textarea with a modern composer.

Example:

   Add a comment...

   ------------------------------------------------
   | Write an update for the support team         |
   |                                              |
   |                                              |
   ------------------------------------------------

   Attach file     Mention @     😊        [Comment]

Make the composer compact and polished.

9. EMPTY STATE

When there are zero comments, don't make the entire section look empty.

Show:

   No comments yet

   Start the conversation by adding the first
   update to this ticket.

Keep it visually subtle.

10. COLOR SYSTEM

Use a refined neutral palette.

Suggested direction:

Background:
#F7F8FA

Surface:
#FFFFFF

Primary text:
#17211B

Secondary text:
#667085

Border:
#E5E7EB

Primary accent:
deep green / emerald

Use semantic colors:

High priority:
subtle red/orange background + darker text

Open:
subtle blue/green background

Pending:
subtle amber background

Resolved:
subtle green background

IMPORTANT:
Use colors sparingly.
Do not make the entire UI green.

11. TYPOGRAPHY

Use a modern UI font such as:

Inter
or
Plus Jakarta Sans

Use a clear type scale.

Avoid the current oversized serif heading.

Suggested:

Page title: 30–34px
Section title: 16–18px
Body: 14–15px
Metadata: 12–13px
Labels: 11–12px

Use font weights carefully.

12. CARDS

Don't put everything inside giant rectangular cards.

Use:
- subtle 1px borders
- 10–14px border radius
- very subtle shadows only where useful
- consistent padding

Create visual grouping through spacing and hierarchy rather than excessive cards.

13. MICRO INTERACTIONS

Add polished interactions:

- button hover
- button press
- input focus
- dropdown animation
- status update feedback
- comment submission feedback
- subtle card hover
- sidebar active-state animation
- skeleton loading where appropriate
- toast notifications

Animations should be subtle and fast.

14. RESPONSIVE DESIGN

Desktop:
Sidebar + main content + ticket information layout.

Tablet:
Collapsible sidebar.

Mobile:
- Sidebar becomes drawer
- Ticket metadata becomes stacked
- Action buttons become full-width where appropriate

15. IMPROVE INFORMATION DENSITY

The screenshot currently wastes too much vertical space.

Make the page fit naturally within a 1080p desktop viewport without requiring excessive scrolling.

The ticket title, metadata, description, status controls, and conversation should feel like one cohesive ticket-detail page.

16. ACCESSIBILITY

Make sure:
- buttons have accessible labels
- keyboard navigation works

- form fields have labels

17. CODE QUALITY

- Do not break existing API integrations.

18. FINAL RESULT

The finished UI should look like a real modern SaaS support platform rather than a basic CRUD application.

Think:

"Linear + Intercom + modern enterprise helpdesk"

rather than:

"basic admin panel with cards and forms".

- Check mobile viewport
